title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Accounting and Finance (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Accounting and Finance (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: National Bank of Ethiopia as a Regulator of financial system do?
options: Create favorable conditions for the expansion of banking, insurance and other financial services
License and supervise banks, insurers and other financial institutions
Make short term and long-term refinancing facilities
questions.explanation: The National Bank of Ethiopia, as a regulator, both creates favorable conditions for financial services expansion (A) and licenses and supervises financial institutions (B).

questions.questionText: If the contribution margin percentage is 30%, the selling price is $5000, then the contribution margin per unit will be?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin per unit = Selling price * Contribution margin percentage = $5000 * 30% = $1,500.

questions.questionText: It is the date on which the entity and another party agree to a share-based payment arrangement?
questions.explanation: The grant date is when the entity and the counterparty agree on the terms of the share-based payment.

questions.questionText: The private organization responsible for establishing the standards for financial accounting and reporting in the United States is called?
options: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA)
questions.explanation: The FASB is responsible for establishing accounting standards in the U.S.

questions.questionText: Within the government-wide financial statements, the column for Business-type Activities will generally include?
questions.explanation: Business-type activities are typically represented by enterprise funds.

questions.questionText: A review of any part of an organization's procedures and methods for the purpose of evaluating efficiency and effectiveness is classified as a(n)?
questions.explanation: An operational audit evaluates the efficiency and effectiveness of an organization's operations.

questions.questionText: According to IAS41 Agriculture, which one of the following items would be classified as biological assets?
questions.explanation: Trees are classified as biological assets under IAS 41 as they are living organisms capable of biological transformation.

questions.questionText: Proprietary fund category is made up of?
options: Internal service fund and Expendable trust fund
Enterprise fund and Expendable trust fund
Enterprise fund and Internal Service fund
Internal service fund and Special Revenue fund
questions.explanation: Proprietary funds consist of enterprise funds and internal service funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about management accounting?
options: It is based on a set of generally accepted accounting principles
questions.explanation: Management accounting focuses on future-oriented reports for internal decision-making.

questions.questionText: When we develop predetermined overhead rate the base should be best cost driver. The underlined phrase implies that?
options: The base inversely related to consumption of overhead cost
Consumption of overhead cost greater than actual
Consumption of overhead less than actual
The base positively related to consumption of overhead cost
questions.explanation: The base should be positively related to the consumption of overhead costs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an argument against regulation?
options: Promote foreign participants in the domestic market
Curb the failure of financial institutions
questions.explanation: Regulation can create moral hazard by encouraging riskier behavior.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a goal of financial regulation?
options: Ensuring the soundness of the financial system
questions.explanation: All listed options are goals of financial regulation.

questions.questionText: What entities shall apply IFRS 11?
options: Only those entities that have joint control over a joint arrangement
Only those entities that have significant influence over a joint arrangement
Only those entities that are a party to a joint arrangement
questions.explanation: IFRS 11 applies to all entities that are a party to a joint arrangement, regardless of whether they have joint control.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about capital markets and securities are true?
options: The maturity of a debt instrument is the time (term) to that instrument's expiration date.
debt instrument is long term if its maturity is ten years or longer.
bond is a long-term security that promises to make periodic payments called dividends to the firm's residual claimants.
questions.explanation: Statements A and B are true regarding capital markets and securities.

questions.questionText: __________ Bonds protect a business against dishonest employees.
questions.explanation: Fidelity bonds protect businesses against losses caused by dishonest employees.

questions.questionText: Which of the following terms are defined by the statement: 'The currency of the primary economic environment in which the entity operates'?
questions.explanation: Functional currency is the currency of the primary economic environment in which the entity operates.

questions.questionText: A form used to appeal raw material from the store to the production center is known as?
questions.explanation: A Material Requisition form is used to request raw materials from the store.

questions.questionText: A debit balance in which of the following accounts would indicate a likely error?
questions.explanation: A debit balance in Fees Earned indicates an error, as it should have a credit balance.

questions.questionText: A group of manufacturing costs referred to as prime costs include?
questions.explanation: Prime costs consist of direct materials and direct labor.

questions.questionText: ………….. Arises when governments borrow when their expenditure is more than revenue?
questions.explanation: Public debt arises when governments borrow to cover expenditures exceeding revenue.

questions.questionText: In April 8, 2013, Trul Corporation purchased merchandise...
questions.explanation: Transaction gain = 10,000 × ($0.60 - $0.45) = $1,500. The gain is recognized when the liability is settled.

questions.questionText: When an investor uses the equity method to account for investments in common stock, cash dividends received by the investor from the investee should be recorded as a?
options: Deduction from the investor's share of the investee's profits
deduction from the stockholders' equity account, dividends to stockholders
questions.explanation: Under the equity method, cash dividends are a return of investment and reduce the investment account.

questions.questionText: The contractually agreed sharing of control of an arrangement, which exists only when decisions about the relevant activities require the unanimous consent of the parties sharing control?
questions.explanation: Joint control exists when decisions require unanimous consent of the parties involved.

questions.questionText: It is important for the auditor to be independent because?
options: The audit conclusions cannot be relied upon if the auditor was biased in accumulating and evaluating evidence
The auditor would not charge a fair rate to the client
The auditor might not be as knowledgeable of the subject matter and the criteria
The Canadian Tax Authorities require that the auditor be independent
questions.explanation: Independence is crucial for the reliability of the audit conclusions.

questions.questionText: Which is the main objective of tax?
questions.explanation: The primary objective of tax is to raise public revenue.

questions.questionText: On April 1, 2016, PP Company paid $950,000...
questions.explanation: Goodwill = Purchase price ($950,000) - Fair value of net identifiable assets ($650,000) = $300,000. Calculated as: Cash $80k + Inventory $190k + PPE $560k - Liabilities $180k = $650k.

questions.questionText: A typical objective of an operational audit is for the auditor to?
options: Determine whether the financial statements fairly present the entity's operations
Evaluate the feasibility of attaining the entity's operational objectives
Report on the entity's relative success in attaining profit maximization
questions.explanation: Operational audits aim to evaluate and improve performance.

questions.questionText: The internal auditor typically reports directly to?
options: The audit committee and the management of the company
The audit committee and the board of director
The board of director and the external auditor
questions.explanation: Internal auditors typically report to the audit committee and the board of directors.

questions.questionText: What are Primary Markets?
options: The amount the seller receives following the sale of an asset after all costs and expenses are deducted.
The value of the assets of the Company or the value of the assets being disposed of, determined without regard to any liabilities associated with such assets.
Where investors buy and sell securities they already own.
Market in which new Securities are issued by the Corporations to raise funds
questions.explanation: Primary markets are where new securities are issued to raise funds.

questions.questionText: __________ is the interest rate at which banks are lending?
questions.explanation: The ask rate (offer rate) is the interest rate at which banks are willing to lend funds.

questions.questionText: During the year an enterprise fund purchased Birr 230,000 worth of equipment...
options: Invested in capital assets, net of related debt is increased by Birr 23,000.
Invested in capital assets, net of related debt is increased by Birr 230,000.
Invested in capital assets, net of related debt is increased by Birr 207,000.
Invested in capital assets, net of related debt is decreased by Birr 207,000.
questions.explanation: Only the down payment (Birr 23,000) increases net assets. The loan portion (Birr 207,000) represents a liability that doesn't affect net asset position.

questions.questionText: The following features characterize process costing except one?
options: Goods are mainly produced to meet customers' orders
Production report is done by department
questions.explanation: Process costing is typically used for continuous production of homogeneous products, not for custom orders.

questions.questionText: Auditing should be done by?
questions.explanation: Auditing should be performed by a competent and independent person.

questions.questionText: On January 1, 2018, Tulema, Inc., reports net assets...
questions.explanation: Patent value: $45,000 - ($45,000/10 years) = $40,500. The 80% acquisition doesn't affect the full value reporting in consolidated statements.

questions.questionText: The process of selling new issues to investors is called?
questions.explanation: Underwriting is the process of selling new issues to investors.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct work flow path in manufacturing industry?
questions.explanation: The correct workflow path is Procurement, Production, Warehousing, and Selling.

questions.questionText: Debt markets used by _____ to raise funds for long-term purposes.
questions.explanation: Both firms/corporations (A) and government (B) use debt markets to raise long-term funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following criteria is not used to classify budget into recurrent & capital budget?
questions.explanation: Source of finance is not a criterion for classifying budgets into recurrent and capital.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true?
options: The issuer of the callable bond reserves the right to call the bonds at particular dates
callable bond is worth more than an identical bond that is non-callable
call obliges the issuer to buy the bonds from the owner
questions.explanation: Only statement A is true. The issuer of callable bonds reserves the right to call the bonds at particular dates. Statement C is incorrect because a call option gives the issuer the right, but not the obligation, to buy back the bonds. Only when the issuer exercises the call option does it become obligated to buy the bonds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following does not represent a primary motivation for business combinations?
options: Quick entry for new and existing products into markets
Combinations as a vehicle for achieving rapid growth and competitiveness
Cost savings through elimination of duplicate facilities and staff
Larger firms being less likely to fail
questions.explanation: Larger firms being less likely to fail is not a primary motivation for business combinations.

questions.questionText: An important financial institution that assists in the initial sale of securities in the primary market is the?
questions.explanation: Investment banks assist in the initial sale of securities in the primary market.

questions.questionText: What type of organizations use auditing services?
questions.explanation: All types of organizations use auditing services.

questions.questionText: This is defined as an arrangement in which two or more parties have joint control?
questions.explanation: A joint arrangement is defined as an arrangement with joint control.

questions.questionText: Which one is not the characteristics of taxation?
options: Benefit may be proportional to tax paid
questions.explanation: The statement 'Benefit may be proportional to tax paid' is not a characteristic of taxation. Taxes are generally not directly tied to benefits received, which distinguishes them from fees or charges for services.

questions.questionText: Fixed assets are double the current assets and half the capital. The current assets are Br.300,000 and investments are Br.400,000. Then, the total liabilities recorded in the balance sheet will be?
questions.explanation: Current Assets = 300,000, Fixed Assets = 2 × 300,000 = 600,000, Investments = 400,000. Total Assets = 1,300,000. Capital = 2 × Fixed Assets = 2 × 600,000 = 1,200,000. Liabilities = Assets - Capital = 1,300,000 - 1,200,000 = 100,000.

questions.questionText: A cost type positively related to volume of production is known as?
questions.explanation: Variable costs are directly related to the volume of production.

questions.questionText: A reason for private companies to be audited is?
options: Having a professional accountant perform their bookkeeping
Complying with the laws requiring them to be audited
Ensuring that their financial statement does not contain errors
questions.explanation: Private companies often seek audits to facilitate access to capital.

questions.questionText: The appropriate journal entry in the accounting records of the home office to record a $20,000 cash remittance in transit from the branch at the end of an accounting period is?
options: Cash in Transit 20,000 Investment in Branch 20,000
questions.explanation: The correct entry reflects the cash in transit as an asset.

questions.questionText: Joe is recording sales transactions in the accounting system so that they can be summarized in a logical manner for the purpose of providing financial information for decision-making. Joe is doing?
questions.explanation: Joe is performing accounting functions by recording sales transactions.

questions.questionText: In the audit of historical financial statements by PA firms, the criteria used are?
options: Regulations of the provincial securities commissions
questions.explanation: Generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) are the criteria used in the audit of historical financial statements. Auditing standards guide how the audit is conducted, but the financial statements themselves are evaluated against accounting principles.

questions.questionText: The governmental body that was established to regulate accounting and auditing profession in Ethiopia in 2015 is?
options: Accounting and Auditing Board of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: The Accounting and Auditing Board of Ethiopia was established to regulate the profession.

questions.questionText: Public expenditure is used to designate the expenditure of?
questions.explanation: Public expenditure refers to expenditures by all levels of government.

questions.questionText: Frankfurter Limited decided that it wanted to improve earnings. To do this, they understated their expenses by omitting unpaid expenses from the accrued liabilities account at year end. Which management assertion has been violated?
questions.explanation: The completeness assertion is violated by omitting unpaid expenses.

questions.questionText: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRSs) are issued by?
options: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA)
questions.explanation: IFRSs are issued by the IASB.

questions.questionText: An accountant records information. When conducting an audit, the distinguishing abilities are?
options: Requirement to possess education beyond the bachelor's degree
Ability to interpret generally accepted accounting principles
questions.explanation: Auditors must accumulate and interpret evidence to form their conclusions.

questions.questionText: In the primary market, the initial time given offers to be public, in financial exchange is considered as?
questions.explanation: The initial public offering (IPO) is the first time a company offers its shares to the public.

questions.questionText: Cost which is sacrificed in choosing the one from two alternatives is known as?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the cost of the next best alternative foregone.

questions.questionText: Federal funds are?
options: Loans made by banks to each other
Loans made by banks to the Federal Reserve System
Funds raised by the federal government in the bond market
Loans made by the Federal Reserve System to banks
questions.explanation: Federal funds are loans made by banks to each other, typically overnight.

questions.questionText: Sineshine Company deducts insurance expense of $21,000 for tax purposes in 2017, but the expense is not yet recognized for accounting purposes. In 2018, 2019 and 2020 taxable income will be higher than financial income because no insurance expense will be deducted for tax purposes, but $7,000 of insurance expense will be reported for accounting purposes in each of these years. Sandy Company has a tax rate of 45% and income taxes payable of $18,000 at the end of 2017. There were no deferred taxes at the beginning of 2017.
options: Income Tax Expense 18,000 Income Tax Liability 18,000
Income Tax Expense 27,450 Income Tax Liability 18,000 Deferred Tax Liability 9,450
Income Tax Expense 26,100 Income Tax Liability 18,000 Deferred Tax Liability 8,100
Income Tax Expense 30,450 Income Tax Liability 21,000 Deferred Tax Liability 9,450
questions.explanation: The tax expense and liability must account for the deferred tax liability due to the timing difference.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the stock exchange?
options: It is a corporation or mutual organization that provides 'trading' facilities for stock traders to trade stock/securities.
It is approved and regulated by the Securities Exchange Commission.
Stocks that are traded on an exchange are individually approved for trading on the exchange by the exchange.
questions.explanation: All statements accurately describe the stock exchange.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accounts typically would be used by an Agency Fund?
questions.explanation: Agency funds typically use cash accounts to manage funds held for others.

questions.questionText: Process Costing System appropriates to?
questions.explanation: Process costing is applicable to all types of continuous production processes.

questions.questionText: Accounting system is used by a business to?
options: Evaluate the performance and health of the business
questions.explanation: Accounting systems serve multiple purposes including analysis, bookkeeping, and performance evaluation.

questions.questionText: If the contribution margin is $13,000, the total variable cost is $7,000 then the total revenue will be?
questions.explanation: Total revenue = Contribution margin + Total variable cost = $13,000 + $7,000 = $20,000.

questions.questionText: The auditor has considerable responsibility for notifying users as to whether or not the statements are properly stated. This imposes upon the auditor a duty to?
options: Be equally responsible with management for the preparation of the financial statements
Be a guarantor of the fairness in the statements
Be an insurer of the fairness in the statements
Provide reasonable assurance that material misstatements will be detected
questions.explanation: Auditors provide reasonable assurance that material misstatements are detected.

questions.questionText: The use of accelerated depreciation for tax purposes and straight-line depreciation for accounting purposes results in?
options: larger amount of depreciation expense shown on the tax return than on the income statement over the asset's useful life.
The asset being fully depreciated for tax purposes in half the time it takes to become fully depreciated for accounting purposes.
larger amount of depreciation expense shown on the income statement than on the tax return in the last year of the asset's useful life.
loss on the sale of the asset in question if it is sold for its book value before its useful life expires.
questions.explanation: In the later years of an asset's life, straight-line depreciation will result in higher expenses on the income statement than accelerated depreciation on the tax return. This is because accelerated methods front-load expenses in early years, leaving less depreciation in later years.

questions.questionText: Which of the following bonds gives the investor the right to sell the bonds to the issuer at par value on designated dates?
questions.explanation: Putable bonds allow investors to sell the bonds back to the issuer at par value on designated dates.

questions.questionText: Which groups of manufacturing costs referred to as conversion costs?
questions.explanation: Conversion costs consist of direct labor and factory overhead, which are the costs to convert raw materials into finished products.

questions.questionText: In a secondary equity market?
options: stock issuing company can raise new capital
Auction is one of the trading mechanisms.
questions.explanation: In the secondary market, trading occurs among investors (option B), and auctions can be a trading mechanism (option C), making option D (B and C) correct.

questions.questionText: ___________ as a group are the net suppliers of funds for financial institutions?
questions.explanation: Individuals as a group are typically the net suppliers of funds to financial institutions through deposits, investments, and other financial products.

questions.questionText: Sikomando Company constructed a warehouse for $280,000 on January 2, 2017. Sikomando estimates that the warehouse has a useful life of 20 years and no residual value. Construction records indicate that $40,000 of the cost of the warehouse relates to its heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system, which has an estimated useful life of only 10 years. What is the first year of depreciation expense using straight-line component depreciation?
questions.explanation: The HVAC system will be depreciated over 10 years, resulting in a first-year expense of $4,000, while the warehouse will be depreciated over 20 years.

questions.questionText: On January 1, 20x1, ABC Co. acquired 60% interest...
questions.explanation: Goodwill = (2,000,000 + 1,080,000) - (6,000,000 - 3,500,000) = 580,000. Includes NCI at fair value and net identifiable assets.

questions.questionText: The auditor must have a thorough understanding of the entity and its environment. The auditor must also consider the client's business strategies, processes, and measurement indicators for critical success factors related to those strategies. This analysis helps the auditor?
options: Decide if they want to accept the engagement
Identify risks associated with the client's strategy that could affect the financial statements
Assess the level of materiality that is appropriate for the audit
Identify the potential for fraud in the financial reporting process
questions.explanation: Understanding the entity and its environment helps auditors identify risks associated with the client's strategy that could affect the financial statements, which is essential for effective audit planning and execution.

questions.questionText: If revenue was $45,000, expenses were $37,500, and the owner's withdrawals were $10,000, the amount of net income or net loss would be?
questions.explanation: Net income is calculated as revenue minus expenses: $45,000 - $37,500 = $7,500. Owner's withdrawals do not affect the calculation of net income.

questions.questionText: Ethiopia has officially adopted the following Accounting Standards but one:
options: IFRSs for Small and Medium Enterprises (IFRS for SME)
questions.explanation: Ethiopia has not officially adopted US Generally Accepted Accounting Standards (GAAPs) as a standard. Instead, it has adopted IFRS, IFRS for SMEs, and IPSASs.

questions.questionText: What is Capital Market?
options: Market in which securities are bought and sold.
financial market in which long-term debt or equity-backed securities are bought and sold.
Entrepreneurs in one country copy an existing market.
market structure defined by a large number of small firms competing against each other.
questions.explanation: Capital markets are financial markets where long-term debt and equity securities are bought and sold, typically with maturities of more than one year.

questions.questionText: The income of the government through all its sources is called?
questions.explanation: Public revenue refers to the income generated by the government from various sources including taxes, fees, fines, and other receipts.

questions.questionText: One of the following inventory valuation methods is not permitted under IFRSs?
questions.explanation: LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) method is not permitted under IFRS as it can understate inventory values and does not reflect the actual flow of inventory in most businesses.

questions.questionText: Which of the following does not represent a primary motivation for business combinations?
options: Combinations as a vehicle for achieving rapid growth and competitiveness.
Cost savings through elimination of duplicate facilities and staff.
Quick entry for new and existing products into markets.
Larger firms being less likely to fail.
questions.explanation: The statement that larger firms are less likely to fail is not a primary motivation for business combinations. Size alone does not guarantee success or prevent failure.

questions.questionText: An important financial institution that assists in the initial sale of securities in the primary market is the?
questions.explanation: Investment banks play a crucial role in the primary market by underwriting and facilitating the initial sale of securities, helping companies raise capital through IPOs and other offerings.

questions.questionText: What type of organizations use auditing services?
questions.explanation: All types of organizations - including non-profit organizations, businesses, and governments - use auditing services to verify financial information and ensure compliance with regulations.

questions.questionText: This is defined as an arrangement in which two or more parties have joint control?
questions.explanation: A joint arrangement is defined as an arrangement where two or more parties have joint control, as specified in IFRS 11.

questions.questionText: Which one is not the characteristics of taxation?
options: Benefit may be proportional to tax paid
questions.explanation: The characteristic that 'Benefit may be proportional to tax paid' is not a characteristic of taxation. Taxes are generally not directly tied to specific benefits received by the taxpayer.

questions.questionText: Fixed assets are double the current assets and half the capital. The current assets are Br.300,000 and investments are Br.400,000. Then, the total liabilities recorded in the balance sheet will be?
A cost type positively related to volume of production is known as?
questions.explanation: Variable costs increase or decrease in direct proportion to the volume of production or activity, showing a positive relationship with production volume.

questions.questionText: A reason for private companies to be audited is?
options: Having a professional accountant perform their bookkeeping
Complying with the laws requiring them to be audited
Ensuring that their financial statement does not contain errors
questions.explanation: Private companies often seek audits to facilitate access to capital, as audited financial statements provide credibility to potential lenders and investors.

questions.questionText: The appropriate journal entry in the accounting records of the home office to record a $20,000 cash remittance in transit from the branch at the end of an accounting period is?
options: Cash in Transit 20,000 Investment in Branch 20,000
questions.explanation: The home office would record: Cash in Transit 20,000, Investment in Branch 20,000. This recognizes the cash that is in transit but not yet received and reduces the investment in branch account.

questions.questionText: Joe is recording sales transactions in the accounting system so that they can be summarized in a logical manner for the purpose of providing financial information for decision-making. Joe is doing?
questions.explanation: Joe is performing accounting functions by recording and summarizing transactions to provide financial information for decision-making, which is the core purpose of accounting.

questions.questionText: In the audit of historical financial statements by PA firms, the criteria used are?
options: Regulations of the provincial securities commissions
questions.explanation: In auditing historical financial statements, the criteria used are generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) or IFRS, as these establish the standards against which financial statements are evaluated.

questions.questionText: The governmental body that was established to regulate accounting and auditing profession in Ethiopia in 2015 is?
options: Accounting and Auditing Board of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: The Accounting and Auditing Board of Ethiopia (AABE) was established in 2015 to regulate the accounting and auditing profession in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Public expenditure is used to designate the expenditure of?
questions.explanation: Public expenditure refers to all spending by public authorities at all levels, including central, state, and local governments.

questions.questionText: Frankfurter Limited decided that it wanted to improve earnings. To do this, they understated their expenses by omitting unpaid expenses from the accrued liabilities account at year end. Which management assertion has been violated?
questions.explanation: The completeness assertion has been violated because the company failed to record all expenses and liabilities that should have been recorded in the financial statements.

questions.questionText: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRSs) are issued by?
options: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA)
questions.explanation: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), which replaced the International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC) in 2001.

questions.questionText: An accountant records information. When conducting an audit, the distinguishing abilities are?
options: Requirement to possess education beyond the bachelor's degree
Ability to interpret generally accepted accounting principles
questions.explanation: When conducting an audit, the distinguishing ability is the accumulation and interpretation of evidence to form an opinion on the fairness of financial statements.

questions.questionText: In the primary market, the initial time given offers to be public, in financial exchange is considered as?
questions.explanation: An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is the first time a company offers its shares to the public in the primary market.

questions.questionText: Cost which is sacrificed in choosing the one from two alternatives is known as?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is foregone when making a choice between alternatives.

questions.questionText: Federal funds are?
options: Loans made by banks to each other
Loans made by banks to the Federal Reserve System
Funds raised by the federal government in the bond market
Loans made by the Federal Reserve System to banks
questions.explanation: Federal funds are short-term loans (typically overnight) made by banks to each other to meet reserve requirements.

questions.questionText: Sineshine Company deducts insurance expense of $21,000 for tax purposes in 2017, but the expense is not yet recognized for accounting purposes. In 2018, 2019 and 2020 taxable income will be higher than financial income because no insurance expense will be deducted for tax purposes, but $7,000 of insurance expense will be reported for accounting purposes in each of these years. Sandy Company has a tax rate of 45% and income taxes payable of $18,000 at the end of 2017. There were no deferred taxes at the beginning of 2017.
options: Income Tax Expense 18,000 Income Tax Liability 18,000
Income Tax Expense 27,450 Income Tax Liability 18,000 Deferred Tax Liability 9,450
Income Tax Expense 26,100 Income Tax Liability 18,000 Deferred Tax Liability 8,100
Income Tax Expense 30,450 Income Tax Liability 21,000 Deferred Tax Liability 9,450
questions.explanation: The deferred tax liability is calculated as $21,000 × 45% = $9,450. The journal entry should be: Income Tax Expense 27,450, Income Tax Liability 18,000, Deferred Tax Liability 9,450.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the stock exchange?
options: It is a corporation or mutual organization that provides 'trading' facilities for stock traders to trade stock/securities.
It is approved and regulated by the Securities Exchange Commission.
Stocks that are traded on an exchange are individually approved for trading on the exchange by the exchange.
questions.explanation: All statements are true about stock exchanges: they provide trading facilities, are regulated by securities commissions, and approve stocks for trading on their platforms.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accounts typically would be used by an Agency Fund?
questions.explanation: Agency funds typically use cash accounts as they primarily hold assets (usually cash) temporarily for other entities or individuals.
